question.text: Ms. Sunita Patil, an SIA empanelled with ICAI SIAB, is drafting a Social Impact Report (SIR) for Pragati Foundation. Which SINGLE item is a MANDATORY component of the SIR irrespective of whether the approach is qualitative or monetary?

answer.text: A description of the scope of the assessment together with assumptions and limitations underlying the analysis
A computed Social Return on Investment (SROI) ratio expressed to two decimal places
A per-beneficiary cost in INR, benchmarked against the Robin Hood Benefit-Cost Ratio
A BACO (Best Available Charitable Option) comparison drawn from Acumen Fund methodology

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook lists the required components of an SIA report, including scope, stakeholder/data-collection details, impact/Theory of Change map, and assumptions and limitations. Scope plus assumptions and limitations is universal across qualitative and monetary approaches. The Trap: SROI, per-beneficiary cost benchmarks and BACO comparisons are linked to quantitative or monetary approaches and are only applicable when such an approach is chosen. Note: Calculations are required only for quantitative or monetary approaches, while scope and assumptions/limitations apply to every SIR.
